minutes.headline: Task force pushes ahead on a stormwater utility fee and the Weston & Samson study contract, with no fee structure voted yet
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force discussed finalizing its consulting contract with Weston and Samson (funded via town meeting) to help design and roll out a townwide stormwater utility fee, including how to tier large commercial properties and whether to credit owners who already maintain their own stormwater controls. No fee structure or utility design was voted on; the board approved October's minutes and adjourned, set the next meeting for January 8th, and heard a resident urge more public education before any fee goes back to town meeting.

what_happened.line: The task force is finalizing its Weston and Samson consulting contract to design a townwide stormwater utility fee, after an initial cost estimate came in too high and the scope was narrowed.
No fee structure or utility design was voted on; discussion of how to tier large commercial properties and whether to credit owners who already maintain stormwater controls ended without resolution.

A resident on Zoom asked whether the consultant contract was competitively bid or awarded sole-source, and urged the task force to hold dedicated public education sessions before any fee goes back to town meeting.
The task force approved October's minutes, skipped a December meeting for the holidays, and set the next meeting for January 8.

why_it_matters: A stormwater utility fee, if the task force eventually proposes one, would be a new charge separate from the property tax levy that residents and businesses would vote on at town meeting.
How the fee tiers large commercial and impervious properties, and whether owners who already maintain their own stormwater controls get credited, will shape who pays more or less.
The contract's public-engagement scope, not yet finalized, will determine how much explanation residents get before being asked to vote on any fee.
